companies.name: OpenAI
companies.context: Raising $40B at $300B valuation led by SoftBank, the largest startup investment ever. Discussed extensively including the history of Sam Altman's 2023 firing and reinstatement and the viral Studio Ghibli image generation moment.

companies.name: SoftBank
companies.context: Investing $40B in OpenAI at $300B valuation, with first $10B financed via Mizuho debt and remaining $30B due by early 2026. S&P Global warned the deal could lead to a credit rating downgrade.

companies.name: Mizuho
companies.context: Japanese bank financing SoftBank's initial $10B OpenAI investment via debt, along with other unnamed lenders.

companies.name: Microsoft
companies.context: Key OpenAI backer; tested GPT-4 in India without informing OpenAI's board or Joint Safety Committee, a breach that contributed to board tensions with Altman.

companies.name: Intel
companies.context: New CEO Lip-Bu Tan two weeks into role with little strategic departure from predecessor; revenue down 33% over four years, Foundry lost $13.4B last year. Analysts suggest splitting design and manufacturing operations.

companies.name: Nvidia
companies.context: Cited as benchmark of chip industry success with $3.5M revenue per employee versus Intel's under $500K.

companies.name: TSMC
companies.context: Superior chip manufacturer that Intel has lost key customers to; TSMC's founder previously worked at Texas Instruments before moving to Taiwan.

companies.name: Google
companies.context: Wrote the transformer paper but failed to vertically integrate research into consumer product as fast as OpenAI; described as having great researchers and product people who weren't communicating.

companies.name: Hermes
companies.context: Hosted the Saut Hermes luxury show jumping competition at Grand Palais in Paris with a 400,000 euro prize; posted 13% sales increase in 2024 despite broader luxury downturn.

companies.name: Meta
companies.context: Discussed for Orion AR glasses demo, Ray-Ban Meta glasses, and Facebook video strategy for creators; Zuckerberg interviewed alongside MrBeast by Samir.

companies.name: TikTok
companies.context: Sale to a US company expected to keep getting punted; described as the biggest search engine for Gen Z and a major economic driver with significant political sway.

companies.name: Citadel
companies.context: Ken Griffin's hedge fund profiled by David Senra; described as most successful hedge fund of all time, founded 35 years ago with over 100K applicants per year.

companies.name: Citadel Securities
companies.context: Market-making arm of Citadel founded 23 years ago; described as a monster business generating massive cash.

companies.name: Anthropic
companies.context: Mentioned as OpenAI competitor; Claude 3 Opus cited by Aidan McLaughlin as his favorite model before joining OpenAI, describing it as having 'big model smell.'

companies.name: Bezel
companies.context: Luxury watch marketplace sponsor; CEO Quaid joining next day to discuss watch market including Rolex Land Dweller, Patek Complications, and AAP launches.

companies.name: Wander
companies.context: Luxury vacation rental sponsor offering homes by the day; used as a humorous analogy for where Sam Altman could have gone to decompress during his firing weekend.

companies.name: Polymarket
companies.context: New official TBPN partner with live ticker on show; praised as superior to traditional news for understanding real probabilities; Circle IPO odds jumped from 54% to nearly 100% after filing.

companies.name: Ramp
companies.context: Show sponsor for corporate card and financial operations; jokingly suggested as solution to Intel's $13.4B Foundry losses.

companies.name: Public.com
companies.context: Show sponsor providing live stock ticker on broadcast; described as multi-asset investing platform trusted by millions.

companies.name: Newsmax
companies.context: Conservative media company that just IPO'd; stock up approximately 1,900% in two days from $10 to over $200, valued beyond $30B; contrasted unfavorably with CoreWeave's cleaner pricing.

companies.name: CoreWeave
companies.context: Cloud computing company that recently IPO'd at exactly $40; praised for not leaving money on the table unlike Newsmax.

companies.name: Circle
companies.context: Filed for IPO; Polymarket odds jumped from 54% to nearly 100% probability of completing a 2025 IPO after the filing was announced.

companies.name: Harvey
companies.context: Mentioned as example of a defensible application-layer AI company that took OpenAI Startup Fund money due to its narrow legal AI vertical.

companies.name: DeepSeek
companies.context: Mentioned for open-sourcing chain-of-thought reasoning approach and creating a discontinuous moment that caused users to re-evaluate OpenAI's most recent models.

companies.name: Mistral
companies.context: Mentioned as one of several open-source GPT-4 level models now available, used to argue that GPT-4 safety concerns were overblown.

companies.name: Manus
companies.context: AI agent product that Aidan McLaughlin defended against 'wrapper' criticism, noting it found uncovered ground despite Operator and Deep Research existing.

companies.name: Waymo
companies.context: Discussed in context of humans mistreating robots; Will DePue predicted it will be safer to use Waymo than Uber within six months.

companies.name: Tesla
companies.context: Autopilot discussed; requires hands on wheel with camera monitoring and a strikes system; mentioned as potential XAI integration target for in-car AI.

companies.name: Figure AI
companies.context: Brett Adcock's humanoid robot company invoked during AI safety debate as hypothetical counter to Eliezer Yudkowsky's doom scenarios.

companies.name: Comma AI
companies.context: George Hotz's self-driving system praised for using a face camera approach instead of requiring hands on wheel; cited as the future direction for self-driving safety.

companies.name: Andreessen Horowitz
companies.context: Marc Andreessen mentioned as putting name in hat for TikTok acquisition.

companies.name: Slow Ventures
companies.context: Sent Dom Perignon bottle to TBPN; described as good friends of the show.

companies.name: Y Combinator
companies.context: Has a stake in OpenAI that PG reportedly learned about via Twitter; OpenAI originated as a YC research project.

companies.name: Airbnb
companies.context: CEO Brian Chesky was a prospective OpenAI board member suggested by Altman; described the board dynamic as 'a bit of a power struggle.'

companies.name: Quora
companies.context: CEO Adam D'Angelo was an independent OpenAI board member during Altman's firing; former Facebook executive.

companies.name: ARM
companies.context: SoftBank portfolio company mentioned as an asset Masayoshi Son could sell to fund the OpenAI investment rather than using debt.

companies.name: Ampere
companies.context: Chip startup acquired by SoftBank for $6.5B as part of its recent offensive pivot in AI.

companies.name: ZBiotics
companies.context: Pre-alcohol probiotic drink company with personal connection to show host; went through YC; co-founders Steven Lam and Zach (CEO) introduced by the host.

companies.name: Numeral
companies.context: Show sponsor providing sales tax compliance for e-commerce and SaaS businesses; works with Ridge, Graza, and 1,000+ other companies.

companies.name: Eight Sleep
companies.context: Smart mattress sponsor; co-founder Mateo announced as upcoming guest to serve as the show's official sleep coach.

companies.name: AdQuick
companies.context: Out-of-home advertising platform sponsor; used by the hosts to post a fake billboard featuring Jeremy Giffon's phone number on the 101 freeway.

companies.name: Notion
companies.context: Launched Notion Mail on April 1st, framing email around a database paradigm, coinciding with Gmail's anniversary.

companies.name: Superhuman
companies.context: Mentioned as example of successful email client that generated FOMO through an invite-only launch strategy.

companies.name: Open Philanthropy
companies.context: EA-aligned charity; Ajay Kotra considered for OpenAI board; Helen Toner was a veteran of the organization.

companies.name: Effective Ventures
companies.context: UK EA charity; board member Tasha McCauley also served on OpenAI's nonprofit board during Altman's firing.

companies.name: Texas Instruments
companies.context: TSMC founder worked there before moving to Taiwan; praised as a great company manufacturing both calculators and weapon systems.

companies.name: Amazon
companies.context: Discussed as a product discovery platform at risk from AI-powered recommendations that align better with consumer interests than ad-based models.

companies.name: Fiverr
companies.context: Will DePue described the 'Fiverr eval' — counting how many gig categories image generation has automated — as his favorite way to measure real-world AI impact.

companies.name: Renaissance Technologies
companies.context: Mentioned in comparison to Citadel's claim as most successful hedge fund; noted Medallion fund was closed to outside investors long ago.

companies.name: Jane Street
companies.context: Briefly mentioned alongside Citadel as a successful trading firm comparison.

companies.name: MidJourney
companies.context: Discussed for its Discord-based prompting community strategy that helped users generate better images through collective inspiration rather than blank text boxes.

companies.name: XAI
companies.context: Elon Musk's AI company mentioned in speculative scenario of integration with Tesla autopilot and X timeline.

companies.name: Hydrazine Capital
companies.context: Sam Altman's first venture fund backed by Peter Thiel; named after rocket fuel that is both a propellant and extremely toxic, seen as a double entendre for venture capital.

companies.name: S&P Global
companies.context: Ratings agency that warned SoftBank's financial condition will likely deteriorate from the OpenAI investment and flagged potential credit rating downgrade.

companies.name: OpenAI Startup Fund
companies.context: Venture fund announced in 2021 to invest in AI startups; Altman personally owned the fund's GP entity for speed but reportedly earned no fees or carry from it.

people.name: David Senra
people.context: Previewed upcoming Ken Griffin/Citadel episode; shared frameworks on killer mentality, technology investment compounding advantages, and finding balance between obsession and personal life using Ed Thorpe as a model.

people.name: Samir Chaudhry
people.context: Discussed creator economy fragmentation, the Zuckerberg and MrBeast joint interview, Facebook video strategy, AI-enhanced vs. fully AI-generated creators, and brand vs. views as a success metric.

people.name: Will DePue
people.role: OpenAI employee, RL post-training and ChatGPT
people.context: Discussed Studio Ghibli viral moment (said OpenAI under-provisioned GPUs), the Fiverr eval for measuring AI utility, robot welfare, and the potential of personalized long-context AI.

people.name: Aidan McLaughlin
people.context: Discussed confusing model naming (plans to unify), deep research as daily practice, Claude 3 Opus as his favorite pre-OpenAI model, AI's bimodal impact on learning, and Manus vs. OpenAI agents.

people.name: Sam Altman
people.context: Central figure in $40B SoftBank fundraise; extensively discussed in book excerpt about his 2023 firing and reinstatement; described as commercially driven, deal-oriented, and the key reason OpenAI can secure this scale of investment.

people.name: Masayoshi Son
people.context: Leading $40B investment in OpenAI using heavy Mizuho debt financing; described as a gambler constantly searching for the next transformational bet who called OpenAI its partner closest to achieving AGI.

people.name: Mira Morati
people.context: Described as an operational mastermind who provided the board with detailed evidence of Altman's management issues via Slack screenshots, then reversed course and led the executive revolt to reinstate him.

people.name: Ilya Sutskever
people.role: Co-founder and former Chief Scientist, OpenAI
people.context: Organized evidence of Altman's alleged deceptions and voted to fire him, but later signed the letter threatening mass resignation if Altman was not reinstated; described as a surprise signatory.

people.name: Greg Brockman
people.context: Described as going around Mira Morati directly to Sam Altman, creating management dysfunction; was also removed from the board during the firing event.

people.name: Peter Thiel
people.context: Mentored Sam Altman and backed his first fund; warned at a birthday dinner that EA-influenced employees would destroy OpenAI; listed as an original OpenAI co-founder.

people.name: Helen Toner
people.role: Former OpenAI board member; Director of Strategy, Georgetown CSET
people.context: Published a paper criticizing OpenAI's approach to safety, angering Altman; key figure in the decision to fire him; caught Altman allegedly lying about safety approvals for GPT-4 features.

people.name: Tasha McCauley
people.role: Former OpenAI board member; former tech CEO
people.context: Effective Ventures board member and wife of Joseph Gordon-Levitt; involved in Altman firing; Altman allegedly falsely told Sutskever that McCauley said Toner should leave the board.

people.name: Adam D'Angelo
people.role: CEO, Quora; former OpenAI board member
people.context: Independent board member present during the secret vote to fire Altman; former Facebook executive.

people.name: Eliezer Yudkowsky
people.context: Funded by Peter Thiel; argued in Time magazine that without halting AI research everyone on Earth will die; described as an AGI doomer whose views influenced EA-aligned OpenAI board members.

people.name: Ken Griffin
people.context: Subject of upcoming Founders episode; described as obsessed with markets since third grade and a 'killer' who chartered a jet to hire Enron talent the day the company collapsed and sent scuba divers to retrieve stolen IP from a Chicago river.

people.name: Ed Thorpe
people.context: Created the first quantitative hedge fund and a wearable computer; gave a 19-year-old Ken Griffin all his files and became Citadel's first LP; cited as a rare positive role model for life balance among great entrepreneurs.

people.name: Lip-Bu Tan
people.context: Two weeks into role; signaling continuity of past strategy while hinting at spinning off non-core businesses; leaning into AI strategy and humanoid robotics as Intel's future direction.

people.name: Pat Gelsinger
people.context: Effectively ousted after ambitious but unsuccessful multi-year effort to improve chip designs and catch manufacturing up to TSMC; described as a 'dog' who embodied Intel's culture of arrogance.

people.name: Brian Chesky
people.context: Was a prospective OpenAI board member suggested by Altman; told the book's author there was 'a bit of a power struggle' because anyone Sam named was automatically suspected of loyalty to Sam.

people.name: John Arnold
people.context: Told the story of Ken Griffin chartering a Gulfstream to Houston the day Enron collapsed to recruit all key trading talent; said he respected Griffin but declined a job while agreeing to speak with him in Aspen.

people.name: Mark Zuckerberg
people.context: Interviewed by Samir alongside MrBeast; discussed Facebook video and creator strategy; gave an Orion AR glasses demo described as one of the craziest tech experiences Samir had ever had.

people.name: MrBeast (Jimmy Donaldson)
people.context: Interviewed alongside Zuckerberg by Samir; discussed using language-agnostic short-form Facebook content and dubbing for global audiences; mentioned as a potential TikTok bidder.

people.name: Jeremy Giffon
people.context: Posted job listing for first hire to work on asymmetric tech special situations; fake billboard with his real phone number was posted on the 101 freeway by the hosts via AdQuick.

people.name: Jacob Pachocki
people.context: Began pursuing a similar research direction to Sutskever's team; after teams merged he took over; his elevation to research director allegedly caused months of lost productivity and internal friction.

people.name: Jessica Livingston
people.context: Has a podcast where she interviewed Sam Altman about the weekend of his firing and reinstatement; recommended as a must-listen.

people.name: Keach Hagey
people.context: Writing 'The Optimist: Sam Altman, OpenAI and the Race to Invent the Future' publishing May 20, 2025; provided a well-sourced account of Altman's firing with access to private dinners and insider accounts.

people.name: George Hotz
people.context: Praised for Comma AI's face-camera-only self-driving approach; argued that monitoring whether a driver is paying attention is superior to requiring hands on the wheel.

people.name: Andy Grove
people.context: Cited as the gold standard of decisive Intel leadership with 'only the paranoid survive'; orchestrated Intel's strategic pivot from memory chips to PC processors in the 1980s.

people.name: Brett Goldstein
people.context: Launched a new all-in-one CRM on April 1st reframing email as a database with applications built on top of it.

people.name: Dworkesh Patel
people.context: Shared Gwern's framework post distinguishing alpha (undiscovered guest/topic) from beta (squeezing more from overexposed guests) interview strategies.

people.name: Andy Grove
people.context: Cited as example of decisive Intel leadership; famous for 'only the paranoid survive' and for pivoting Intel from memory to processors in the 1980s.

people.name: Ajay Kotra
people.context: Interviewed as a potential OpenAI board member; process stalled due to alleged foot-dragging by Altman and Brockman.

topics.name: SoftBank $40B OpenAI Investment
topics.summary: SoftBank investing $40B in OpenAI at $300B valuation, the largest startup investment ever. First $10B financed via Mizuho debt with remaining $30B due by early 2026. S&P Global warned it could deteriorate SoftBank's financial condition and trigger a credit rating downgrade. Hosts debated whether debt-financed equity in a pre-profit AI company is genius or reckless.

topics.name: Sam Altman Firing and Reinstatement
topics.summary: Detailed account from Keach Hagey's forthcoming book describing board's secret November 2023 vote to fire Altman, Mira Morati's dual role providing evidence then leading executive revolt, Ilya Sutskever's surprise reversal, and near-unanimous employee threat to quit. Hosts criticized the book's analysis while praising its sourcing.

topics.name: OpenAI Studio Ghibli Image Generation
topics.summary: New image generation in ChatGPT went massively viral with Studio Ghibli-style artwork. Will DePue said OpenAI under-provisioned GPUs and was surprised by demand. Aidan said Sam and leadership had well-calibrated intuitions about virality. Hosts praised it as a crossing-the-chasm moment for mainstream AI adoption.

topics.name: Intel Turnaround Strategy
topics.summary: New CEO Lip-Bu Tan two weeks into role, largely continuing predecessor's strategy while hinting at non-core spinoffs and humanoid robotics pivot. Intel revenue down 33% over four years with Foundry losing $13.4B last year and revenue per employee far below Nvidia. Analysts advocate for splitting design and fab operations.

topics.name: Ken Griffin and Citadel
topics.summary: David Senra previewed upcoming Founders episode on Ken Griffin; discussed his killer mentality, recruiting all key Enron traders on the day of collapse, founding relationship with Ed Thorpe, the IP theft river recovery story, and building multiple business verticals over 35 years by maxing out TAM in each one.

topics.name: Creator Economy and AI
topics.summary: Samir Chaudhry discussed 47% of Gen Z stat on fragmented fandom, brand vs. views distinction, Facebook video and DM-sharing as unit of conversation, and AI-enhanced versus fully AI-generated creators. Notebook LM cited as most compelling AI audio content; VTubers cited as growing category.

topics.name: TikTok Sale
topics.summary: Expected to keep getting punted; no clear buyer emerging with Andreessen Horowitz and Alexis Ohanian's Project Liberty among candidates. Described as biggest Gen Z search engine, major ad revenue driver, and significant political communications platform whose status is deeply uncertain.

topics.name: AI Safety and Effective Altruism at OpenAI
topics.summary: Extensive discussion of EA influence on OpenAI board, Eliezer Yudkowsky's doom predictions funded by Peter Thiel, structural misalignment between nonprofit board and consumer tech company trajectory, Helen Toner's outside safety paper, and the board's non-technical governance of technically transformational products.

topics.name: OpenAI Product Strategy and Model Design
topics.summary: Will and Aidan discussed viral image generation, confusing model naming with plans to unify, deep research as a daily practice, Manus as a valid non-wrapper agent product, and the bimodal impact of AI on learning. Both expressed excitement about personalization and proactive AI as the next frontier.

topics.name: Newsmax IPO
topics.summary: Conservative media company Newsmax went public and surged approximately 1,900% in two days from $10 to over $200, valuing it beyond $30B. Contrasted with CoreWeave's cleaner IPO pricing. Hosts noted leaving money on the table at IPO.

topics.name: Circle IPO Filing
topics.summary: Circle officially filed for an IPO; Polymarket prediction market odds jumped from 54% to nearly 100% probability of completing a 2025 IPO immediately after the filing was announced.

topics.name: Luxury Watches
topics.summary: Bezel sponsor segment highlighted a wave of new watch launches including Rolex Land Dweller, Patek Complications watch over $1M, and Audemars Piguet updates. Piaget Polo 79 in white gold at ~$100K highlighted as a lot of watch for the money.

topics.name: Hermes Equestrian Competition
topics.summary: Annual Saut Hermes show jumping competition at Grand Palais Paris with 400,000 euro grand prize; 110 horses competed with chandeliers matching the brand's flagship store. Hermes posted 13% sales increase in 2024 despite luxury downturn attributed to heritage positioning.

topics.name: Autonomous Vehicles and Robot Welfare
topics.summary: Will DePue predicted Waymo will be safer than Uber in six months; Comma AI's face-camera approach praised over Tesla's hands-on-wheel requirement. Will raised the issue of model welfare as AI systems grow more complex, expressing concern about humans mistreating robots and AI.

topics.name: Prediction Markets as News Signal
topics.summary: Hosts advocated using Polymarket as a filter for when news actually matters, proposing a model where you only read deep dives when market odds shift significantly rather than consuming continuous PR-driven coverage.

key_claims: SoftBank's $40B OpenAI investment is the largest investment ever made in a startup.
S&P Global warned SoftBank's financial condition will likely deteriorate from the OpenAI investment and may lead to a credit rating downgrade.
Intel's annual revenue has shrunk 33% over the last four years; its Foundry business lost $13.4B last year.
Nvidia generates approximately $3.5M revenue per employee versus Intel's under $500K.
Will DePue (OpenAI) said OpenAI under-provisioned GPUs for the Studio Ghibli image generation launch, indicating demand was higher than internal models predicted.
Aidan McLaughlin (OpenAI) said OpenAI plans to unify and simplify its model selection interface soon.
47% of Gen Z are fans of something on the internet that no one they know personally is also a fan of (YouTube-sourced stat cited by Samir Chaudhry).
The most subscribed Twitch streamer at the end of 2024 was Ironmouse, a VTuber (virtual animated creator).
Newsmax stock rose approximately 1,900% in two days post-IPO, from $10 to over $200 per share, valuing it beyond $30B.
Circle officially filed for an IPO; Polymarket odds jumped from 54% to nearly 100% probability for a 2025 IPO.
Will DePue predicted it will be safer to use Waymo than Uber within six months.
Aidan McLaughlin predicted AI will have a bimodal impact on students: bottom percentile will fall further behind while top percentile becomes vastly more capable.
David Senra said Ken Griffin had over 100,000 people apply to work at Citadel in a single year.
Sam Altman personally owned the GP of the OpenAI Startup Fund but reportedly earned no fees or carry from it.
Nearly 800 OpenAI employees threatened to quit if Sam Altman was not reinstated after his November 2023 firing.
Microsoft tested GPT-4 in India without informing OpenAI's board or receiving Joint Safety Committee approval, and no one informed the board until an employee mentioned it in a hallway.
Hermes posted a 13% sales increase in 2024 versus 2023 despite a broader luxury market downturn.
Aidan McLaughlin described Claude 3 Opus as having 'big model smell' and called it his favorite model before joining OpenAI.
Sam Altman was an investor in Stripe when Greg Brockman was its CTO, predating their OpenAI co-founding relationship.
Ed Thorpe gave a 19-year-old Ken Griffin all his files and became Citadel's first LP, enabling the fund's early convertible debt strategy.
